skill: Differentiate square-root and reciprocal-square-root functions of linear or quadratic polynomials using the chain rule; in slope questions evaluate the derivative at a specified point.
reasoning_steps: Identify inner polynomial u and outer power 1/2 or -1/2.
Differentiate outer and inner functions separately and multiply.
Substitute the original polynomial and simplify.
For tangent-slope tasks, evaluate at the stated x; differentiate an added cubic separately when present.
response_contract: Radio with five complete options or a mathematical blank. Blank choice histories include incomplete learner entries, not alternative correct answers. Canonical example has no answer field.
difficulty: Captured easy questions evaluate slopes, including quadratic radicands, a zero stationary slope, reciprocal roots, and one radical-plus-cubic sum. Moderate/hard symbolic derivative families must retain their captured difficulty; missing difficulty on q-48846 needs a documented inference.
invariants: Outer exponent is plus/minus one half; inner polynomial degree at most two in this KP.
Real differentiable evaluation points require positive radicand.
Derivative contains the inner derivative factor, including legitimate zero at a stationary point.
Preserve symbolic versus evaluated response and observed radio versus blank profiles.
One chain-rule application, plus the observed cubic derivative only for its source family.
permitted_variations: Small coefficients, signs, constants and evaluation points while maintaining valid domain and comparable arithmetic.
Positive, negative and zero slopes where inner polynomial permits them.
For fixed quadratic, change evaluation target and recompute all dependent solution and answer content.
Vary radio position and distractor values without a template cue identifying the answer.
An additive constant outside the radical can vary without changing the derivative; this is a mathematical counterfactual, not a required production extension.
source_refs: tutorial 743ad997-8732-5c0f-9676-ff1d44f3b513, Introduction: decompose f(g)=g^3, g(x)=1+2x; multiply df/dg by dg/dx, then substitute.
lesson step 60f88dd0-c1bd-546f-9dac-f440401fd02b: e-182 uses u=1-x^2, dy/du=1/(2 sqrt(u)), du/dx=-2x.
essential_vs_incidental: The chain-rule dependency is essential; particular coefficient signs, zero/nonzero outcomes, correct option position, and evaluation x are incidental. A zero-slope source does not justify always placing quadratic targets at the vertex.
gaps: q-48846 lacks correct-answer link, solution and difficulty; mathematical key is 2/sqrt(4x-3), independently inferred.
